title: Do you actually trust AI when making trading decisions?
author: ibrahimdigital
selftext:
I've been seeing more and more AI trading tools lately and I'm honestly curious how people here use them.

Do you actually let AI influence your trades or is it just another source of ideas that you verify yourself?

I've tried a few tools, and while some generate interesting setups, I still find myself double-checking everything before entering a position.

For those who've been using AI for a while:

* Has it genuinely improved your results?
* Do you use it every day or only in certain market conditions?
* What's one feature you wish AI trading tools did better?

I'm interested in hearing real experiences- the good, the bad and the disappointing.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body:
The main issue with most AI trading tools is that the quality of the analysis depends entirely on the data you feed into the model. A generic ChatGPT or Claude prompt usually pulls from shallow, free public market data—think Yahoo-style fundamentals—which isn't deep enough for serious stock selection. That’s why you end up double-checking everything.

I’ve found that the better first layer is a platform like trademates.co, which uses enterprise-level API access plus an in-house weighting model to score and structure the data before the LLM even analyzes it. That produces far more structured output than random prompts into a chatbot. It’s still a source of ideas you verify yourself, but the signal-to-noise ratio is much higher because the data foundation is stronger.

comments.author: Good_Character_20
comments.body: For me the AI part was never the hard part. Generating a strategy that looks great on historical data is easy, almost too easy. I run an AI loop that produces a few hundred candidates a week, and the honest result is that most of them are garbage that just curve-fit the training window. The value isn't in trusting the output, it's in what happens after. I treat every AI-generated strategy as guilty until proven innocent. It has to clear out-of-sample testing, walk-forward across several windows, and a Monte Carlo check against shuffled price data before I take it seriously. Around ninety percent don't survive that. The ones that do haven't earned my trust either, they've just earned a paper-trading slot. So no, I don't let AI influence a trade directly. It proposes, the validation decides.

comments.author: TacticalDataDesk
comments.body:
Yes I trust it. I've handed my account over to an AI driven trading bot two weeks ago. Haven't had a problem.

  
I developed the bot myself.

comments.author: silphotographer
comments.body:
Simple and only answer is: you cannot.

If you think you can, then you're crazy.

But it can help with the automation process so that a competent trader can analyze and optimize more effectively with well-trained LLM.
